cohort: 1381 women, divided into groups based on consanguineous and non-consanguineous marriages, and their newborn babies, from a military hospital in Rawalpindi.
finding: Consanguineous marriages were significantly associated with a higher risk of adverse neonatal outcomes, including neonatal intensive care unit admission, stillbirth, perinatal mortality, and congenital abnormalities.
followup_time: up to discharge from the hospital
